body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s a warm Wednesday, August 26, 2026, and our top story today is the announcement that Kern County Sheriff Donny Youngblood will retire in January 2027 after serving 20 years as our sheriff. We’re also keeping an eye on the weather as temperatures climb to 102° today with moderate air quality. Let’s take a look at what happened overnight, what’s making news, and what’s coming up this week.

## The Kern Overnight

Overnight activity was relatively light across Kern County, though a few notable incidents kept law enforcement busy. Around 9:18 p.m., officers responded to repeated intruder reports on the 2400 block of South M Street. A resident barricaded himself in his bathroom with his dog after an unknown subject was reported attempting to enter his apartment for a fourth time. The situation kept officers on scene into the evening. Elsewhere, at 22:17, a juvenile fled in a vehicle in Bakersfield, prompting a brief search. A family member followed but had not yet provided a direction of travel or a description of the vehicle. Later, at 05:09, police staged for a subject experiencing a mental-health crisis on the 2800 block of University Avenue. Overall, the night was calm with no major incidents reported elsewhere in the county.

## Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for a high near 102° and a low around 75° tonight. It’s currently 99° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and there are no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 87. Be sure to stay hydrated and take precautions if you’ll be outdoors for extended periods.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that two individuals have been charged following a shooting at Independence High School.** The incident has raised concerns about safety on campus, and school officials are working closely with law enforcement to ensure that measures are in place to protect students and staff. The charges come as the community grapples with the aftermath of the shooting, and discussions about security enhancements are expected in the coming weeks.

**Bakersfield Now tells us that the driver accused in a deadly wrong-way crash on Highway 99 worked at North Kern State Prison.** The crash, which resulted in fatalities, has sparked questions about road safety and the potential for impaired driving. Authorities are continuing their investigation into the incident, and any findings will be crucial in understanding how to prevent similar tragedies in the future.

**According to 23ABC, the California City Council denied two appeals challenging the approval of the CoreCivic ICE detention facility.** The appeals argued that immigration detention is not the same as a prison or correctional facility and is not a permitted use under the city's zoning code. Despite these challenges, the council voted 4-1 to deny both appeals, allowing the facility to continue operating under its existing approvals. The decision has sparked debate about the role of such facilities in the community and the interpretation of local zoning laws.

**KGET 17 also shared that the trial for a Bakersfield crash that killed a married couple is expected to begin by October.** The case has been closely watched by the community, and the upcoming trial will be an important step in seeking justice for the victims. Details of the crash and the circumstances surrounding it will likely come to light as the trial progresses, and the outcome may have implications for traffic safety measures in the area.

## Something good

In a delightful community event, a local Bakersfield bakery is honoring Dolly Parton with special sweet treats. The bakery is celebrating the iconic singer’s contributions to child literacy through a variety of desserts that pay homage to her work. It’s a heartwarming gesture that brings a smile to our faces and reminds us of the power of community spirit.

## Coming up this week

There are several public meetings and events worth noting this week. Today, August 26, there will be a Special City Council Meeting at 12:00 p.m., followed by a City Council Meeting 330 at 3:30 p.m. and a City Council Meeting 515 at 5:15 p.m. On September 2, the Personnel and Processes Committee will meet at 12:00 p.m. For entertainment, mark your calendars for Brit Floyd at Mechanics Bank Arena on October 13 at 8:00 p.m. and Los Tigres Del Norte at the same venue on October 16 at 8:00 p.m. These events offer great opportunities to engage with our community and enjoy some local culture.
